elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may make termination effective on 30 days' written notice, without an additional month-end timing restriction.
elements.evidence: Although subsection (a) requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, termination remains restricted to the end of a calendar month, so 30 days' notice may not be sufficient to make termination effective.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right is not subject to an early-termination fee or penalty.
elements.evidence: The added sentence says termination is “without penalty,” but subsection (b) still requires payment of applicable early termination charges. The operative provisions conflict and do not clearly eliminate such charges.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of fees prepaid for the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: IBM must refund any Charges prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination, which provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that IBM may not terminate the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience during any committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's required notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only at least 30 days' prior written notice, subject to calendar-month-end effectiveness; it does not establish a 60–90 day notice requirement.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) incorporates early termination charges from the attachments without any three-month cap. The later “without penalty” sentence creates a contradiction rather than an enforceable cap.
The clause does not affirmatively grant IBM a termination-for-convenience right; it only prohibits such termination during a committed term.

elements.element: Vendor's termination-for-convenience right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: A prohibition during a committed term does not expressly limit any permitted IBM termination to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice obligation applies to any IBM termination for convenience.

result.reason: The redline does not reach either position. For the preferred position, the calendar-month-end restriction can extend Customer's notice period beyond 30 days, and the retained obligation to pay early termination charges directly conflicts with the new “without penalty” language. The fallback notice period, fee cap, and IBM end-of-term/90-day termination framework are also absent. The internal penalty contradiction prevents the clause from preserving intent cleanly, and the redline is not minimal to a complete acceptable position because necessary deletions or conforming revisions were omitted.
